methodology.timer: time.perf_counter_ns around complete subprocess; timeout 180 seconds
methodology.timing_order: Six rounds, all six permutations of three versions; each version appears twice in every position per workload. No concurrent build/test/probe job.

diagnostics.snapshot: Process-global diagnostic counters sampled at RuntimeInner::drop entry; final snapshot excludes the final Runtime teardown itself. Multiple snapshots, if present, are cumulative and are not added together.
diagnostics.counters: Relaxed AtomicU64 counters in separate source copies. Never use these builds for performance claims.
diagnostics.cpu: Uninstrumented production binaries; perf cycles:u at 499 Hz, no call graph. Leaf symbol periods only; inlined work can be attributed to its containing symbol.

limitations: No controlled CPU frequency or full system isolation.
Whole-process timing includes initialization, compilation, execution and teardown.
Property workload includes numeric loop/accumulation work.
Perf samples are leaf symbols, not inclusive call graphs; inline attribution can move. CPU runs are grouped by version and are used for attribution, not timing claims.
Diagnostic counts use separate instrumented source copies; never interpret their execution time as production performance.
Two Cell<bool> flags added per Runtime; no separate allocation. No memory/phase timing probe.
Empty loop does not establish a gain; a small regression remains possible.
Final wrapper lint annotations and documentation do not change measured runtime logic.
